correctness.rationale: The actions of the residue field on m/m² and m² require no embedded coefficient field: changing a scalar lift adds an element of m, and the error vanishes in the corresponding quotient. Multiplication descends and is nonzero because products span m². The radical lifts to Ann(m), of size q^(r+1); its nonzero elements are universal. A nonradical element has a nonorthogonal partner in the quotient and the partner has at least two lifts, ensuring a distinct nonneighbor. Each nonzero projective direction of the nondegenerate quotient has q^(r+1)(q-1) lifts, a clique for isotropic directions and an independent set otherwise. Rank one gives a single independent fiber; rank two gives fixed points or transposed pairs of the projective perpendicularity involution. The binary forms have the stated isotropic-point counts, including char 2 where the diagonal quadratic polynomial is a square of a linear form. The components, clique joins and colorings follow. In odd characteristic diagonalization supplies an orthogonal triple. In finite characteristic two nonalternating, split off nonisotropic lines; any residual nonzero alternating summand decomposes into hyperbolic planes. Combining one diagonal line with one plane, normalized to B(e,e)=B(u,v)=1, gives three orthogonal nonisotropic vectors e+u,e+v,e+u+v, and the construction can absorb additional planes if needed. In the diagonal triple the five consecutive pairings vanish and the other five are c_0,-c_0,d,-c_0,a. The alternating two-plane-pair formula has all consecutive pairings zero and all nonconsecutive ones equal to one in characteristic two. The vectors give distinct projective points and distinct ring-vertex lifts, so C5 is induced with clique number 2 and chromatic number 3. The filtration gives |R|=q^(r+t+2); the rank-three F2 model has unit, associative multiplication since all triple products in m vanish, and realizes equality 32. The frozen verification note and prime-field script were inspected, not executed. The 13 reported finite checks neither cover arbitrary fields or mixed characteristic nor replace the intrinsic proof.

The extraspecial result dd5cf5a0520d gives symplectic rank-one perfectness and explicit two-hyperbolic-pair C5; the Gorenstein result 3dd8b506381f gives the exact rank-two decomposition including both characteristics and all fixed-point counts.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Universality and chromatic boundedness alone do not imply the threshold. But the explicit scalar symplectic cycle uses only field constants in F2 when specialized to characteristic two, so choosing two such pairs works over every finite field of characteristic two, with any radical. The rank-two formula supplies the base with no radical, and the quotient fibers give the rest.

evidence: ER_q is exactly the induced projective graph on an orthogonal triple; its Petersen subgraph for q>=3 and C4-freeness are sufficient. The extraspecial alternating C5 proof lists five vectors in two hyperbolic pairs, with all cross decisions nonzero on nonedges even at p=2. The rank-two Gorenstein formula uses the same perpendicular line involution.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: For rank two, choose the split model with the quotient form to match the Gorenstein theorem, then replace each isotropic point fiber by a clique and each anisotropic fiber by an independent set of q^r times the old size; change the universal count to q^(r+1)-1. Orthogonal paired fibers still give complete bipartite components. Rank one is the single nonisotropic projective point. Higher rank embeds the respective existing 3D orthogonal or 4D symplectic obstruction. Together with the seven-point q=2 check, these imply the complete threshold. The order bound then follows immediately from t>=3 and the length formula, with the smallest graded diagonal model realizing it; this does not constitute a separate census.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Restrict a nonalternating nondegenerate form of rank >=3 to a nondegenerate orthogonal triple. In dimension three over odd q every form is similar to the dot product (scale to the determinant class, then use finite-field binary/ternary classification); over even q diagonal coefficients may all be scaled to 1 by square roots. Scalar similarity preserves perpendicularity. A Petersen C5 has no chord in ER_q since any chord in a five-cycle creates a four-cycle. The q=2 omission is only the seven points of PG(2,2), where the ordered binary vectors 001,010,101,111,110 have zero dot products just along the cycle. Representatives of five directions in the ring preserve all induced adjacencies.

originality.rationale: The main threshold assembles already covered projective-orthogonality cases. The key nonalternating rank-three obstruction is the classical graph ER_q, not a new graph family; the 2014 Tait–Timmons Petersen-subgraph theorem plus C4-freeness forces an induced C5 for every q>=3, and the remaining ER_2 is a seven-point graph with an immediate five-point check. Every higher nonalternating rank contains this three-dimensional projective subgraph. The distinct indexed extraspecial symplectic construction already provides the alternating obstruction, and the distinct indexed Gorenstein rank-two decomposition lifts directly to arbitrary radical by the projective fiber counts. Neither lack of coefficient-field embedding nor mixed characteristic changes any of these adjacency decisions. The explicit coordinate witness and length-filtration cutoff are useful self-contained deductions, but no independently distinct structural regime survives the comparison. This judgment credits precise coverage, not chronology of later catalogue entries, and is not based on inaccessible texts.
residual_risks: Exact full-text overlap with the 2017 perfect zero-divisor graphs article and Bloomfield’s order-p^5 paper is unresolved, not evidence of noncoverage or failure.
